m:colosseo: From outside it's free. To get in you need a named ticket (€18 for the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine, valid 24 hours) and ID: it's sold only on colosseo.it, 30 days ahead, and on the day it's often sold out.
m:campidoglio: The square and the viewpoint over the Forum are free. The Vittoriano's ground floor is free to visit; the panoramic terrace at the top is paid.
m:pantheon: Entry costs €5. Open every day 9am–7pm (last entry 6:30pm); during Saturday evening and Sunday morning Mass tourist access may be limited.
m:navona: The Campo de' Fiori market is open Monday to Saturday until midday. At Navona and in the surrounding streets beware of restaurants with waiters who stop you: to eat, move into the side alleys.
m:trevi: Since 2 February 2026 it costs €2 to get close to the basin (free for residents of Rome and its province). Open 9am–10pm, Fridays from 11:30am, last entry 9pm; after closing you can look from the square, for free. There are always pickpockets.
m:spagna: Sitting on the steps is forbidden (fines up to €250). The boutiques line Via dei Condotti: looking is the only thing that's free.
m:sanpietro: Free entry. Shoulders and knees covered, no exceptions. The basilica is open 7am–6:30pm (from October); on Wednesday mornings it closes for the Pope's audience. Climbing the dome costs about €10 on foot or €15 with the lift, until 4:30pm.
m:trastevere: The basilica is free and open until the evening. In the evening the neighbourhood fills up and the places on the squares cost more: the good ones are in the alleys.
m:ghetto: All free. Try the ricotta and sour cherry tart from the Boccione bakery and, in season, carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes).
m:colosseoins: Named ticket from €18 on colosseo.it, on sale 30 days ahead, valid 24 hours (one entry to the Colosseum and one to the archaeological area). The Colosseum opens at 8:30am, the Forum and Palatine at 9am; until 24 October closing is at 6:30pm, from 25 October at 4:30pm (last entry an hour before). Free entry on 4 November and the first Sunday of the month.
m:vaticani: Ticket €20 plus €5 to book a time slot: on the official website museivaticani.va. Closed on Sundays, except the last of the month (free, mornings only, with very long queues), and on 1 November. In the Sistine Chapel keep silent and no photos; shoulders and knees covered.
m:castel: Ticket €16. Open every day 9am–7:30pm (entry until 6:30pm). You can see it well from the bridge without going in.
m:gianicolo: Free and always open. The climb from Trastevere is steep (about 20 minutes on foot); alternatively there's bus 115.
m:borghese: Booking a time slot is compulsory (€16 plus €2 booking fee) on galleriaborghese.it, and the visit lasts two hours with fixed entry slots. Closed on Mondays. Arrive half an hour early to collect your ticket.
m:pincio: Free. The park closes to vehicles at sunset, but the paths stay open; the Pincio terrace is always open.
m:aventino: The garden is free, open until sunset. For the keyhole there's usually a queue of a few minutes.
m:bocca: For the Mouth of Truth there's a voluntary donation (usually €1–2) and often a queue. The Circus Maximus can be seen for free from the edge.
m:caracalla: Ticket €8. Closed on Mondays. Hours follow daylight and change with the seasons: in autumn they close before sunset, check on coopculture.it.
m:testaccio: The market is open Monday to Saturday, 7am–3:30pm, closed on Sundays; stalls close early, best to arrive by noon.
vd:serpenti: A neighbourhood bakery in Monti: pizza al taglio by weight, supplì and sweets, with self-service coffee from the machine. Eat standing or at the narrow tables.
vp:serpenti: A slice of pizza and a coffee stay under €6 (menu not seen).
vd:mary: A micro-bakery with an ice-cream counter on the little square with the Monti fountain: cornetti, pizza bianca, sandwiches and ice cream until late.
vp:mary: Breakfast or a snack under €6 (menu not seen).
vd:panmonti: A neighbourhood bakery: bread, pizza bianca, biscuits and baked sweets. Closed on Sundays.
vd:licata: The Monti locals' bar: breakfast at the counter with cornetti and coffee, sandwiches and an aperitivo at the end of the day. On Mondays it closes at 2:30pm.
vp:licata: Cappuccino and cornetto at the counter around €3–4 (menu not seen).
vd:roscioli: The historic bakery near Campo de' Fiori: white and red pizza, supplì, pastries. Say how big a piece you want and they weigh it. There's often a bit of a queue but it moves.
vp:roscioli: A slice of pizza and a pastry stay under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:campofiori: A bakery on the market square: pizza bianca filled with mortadella or ham, to eat as you walk. Closed on Sundays.
vp:campofiori: A pizza bianca sandwich under €7 (menu not seen).
vd:supplizio: Supplì fried to order: the classic al telefono (with the string of mozzarella), cacio e pepe and carbonara. Few chairs; eat standing or on the little square. Closed on Sundays.
vp:supplizio: A supplì costs about €3.50–4: three and a drink stay under €15 (from reviews).
vd:coronari: A small place for supplì and fresh pasta made to order, with a cheerful room where you sign the table with a marker. Closed on Tuesdays.
vd:boccione: A Jewish bakery for over 200 years, with no sign: ricotta and sour cherry tart, ricotta and chocolate tart, almond sweets. Sold by weight. Closed on Saturdays.
vp:boccione: A slice costs a few euros (menu not seen).
vd:baffetto: A historic pizzeria a short walk from Piazza Navona: round Roman pizza, thin and crispy, one each. Cash only and there's a queue. Closed on Tuesdays.
vp:baffetto: A margherita around €8 and a beer: under €15 (from reviews, cash only).
vd:parenti: A neighbourhood pâtisserie near Ottaviano metro, 8 minutes from the Vatican: cornetti, maritozzi and baked sweets. Closed on Mondays.
vd:cornetteria: A cornetto workshop in Prati, open almost round the clock: hot cornetti with custard, chocolate or jam, for night owls too.
vp:cornetteria: A cornetto costs about €1.50 (menu not seen).
vd:pizzarium: Gabriele Bonci's pizza al taglio near the Vatican Museums: long-fermented dough and seasonal toppings, sold by weight. Take a number and wait, often for a while.
vp:pizzarium: Two pieces and a drink around €12–15; paid by weight (from reviews).
vd:suegiu: A family trattoria in Prati, frequented by locals: carbonara, cacio e pepe, gricia, gnocchi and tripe. Closed on Sundays.
vp:suegiu: A pasta course costs about €10–13 (from reviews): with just pasta and water it's around €15.
vd:levain: A French-style bakery in Trastevere: flaky croissants, sourdough bread and filter coffee.
vd:checco: The pâtisserie and bar of the historic Trastevere restaurant, open from morning till night: cornetti filled with pistachio cream, ice cream and sweets.
vp:checco: Cornetto and cappuccino around €4–5 (menu not seen).
vd:aimarmi: A pizzeria for Romans, also called «L'Obitorio» (the morgue) for its marble tables: thin pizza, supplì and courgette flowers. You wait in the street. Closed on Wednesdays.
vp:aimarmi: Two pizzas and a bottle of water around €22, so about €11 each (from reviews).
vd:darpoeta: A pizzeria in the alley behind Piazza Trilussa: pizza with a softer dough, bruschetta and supplì. Open every day.
vp:darpoeta: A pizza around €8–11; with a beer you stay under €15 (from reviews).
vd:nannarella: A trattoria on Piazza San Calisto: egg pasta and Roman pasta dishes, like amatriciana, carbonara and gricia, with generous portions.
vp:nannarella: A pasta course costs about €12–14 (from reviews): with just pasta and water it's around €15.
vd:regoli: A pâtisserie in the Esquilino, 15 minutes' walk from Termini: excellent cream maritozzi and strawberry tart. The till is separate from the counter. Closed on Tuesdays.
vp:regoli: A maritozzo costs about €4.50 (from reviews): breakfast around €7–8.
vd:cecio: A trattoria a short walk from Termini but for Esquilino locals: simple Roman dishes, like amatriciana, gricia and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew).
vp:cecio: A pasta course costs about €9–12 (menu not seen).
vd:manzoni: A trattoria near the Manzoni metro A stop, between the Esquilino and San Giovanni: hearty Roman cooking, open all day.
vd:fornotrevi: A bakery a short walk from the fountain: cornetti filled with chocolate or pistachio at honest prices, always a bit of a queue but quick.
vp:fornotrevi: A cornetto around €2.50–3 (from reviews, takeaway only).
vd:trecaffe: A modern café near Piazza di Spagna: pistachio maritozzi, croissants and good coffee, for brunch too.
vp:trecaffe: Breakfast at the counter around €6–8 (menu not seen).
vd:guerra: Fresh pasta to take away a short walk from the Trinità dei Monti steps: two dishes every day, one meat and one vegetarian, to eat standing or on the steps of the square.
vp:guerra: A dish costs about €4–5 with water included (from reviews).
vd:remo: A Romans' pizzeria in Testaccio: thin round pizza and supplì, crowded tables and noise. No bookings. Closed on Sundays.
vp:remo: A pizza around €8–10; with a beer you stay under €15 (from reviews).
vd:mercatotest: The neighbourhood's covered market, with stalls serving porchetta or tripe sandwiches, supplì and dishes of the day to eat among the stalls. Closed on Sundays.
cd:capitolini: The world's oldest museums, on the Capitoline Hill: the Capitoline Wolf, Marcus Aurelius and a terrace over the Forums.
cd:callisto: Underground galleries with the tombs of early Christian popes and martyrs, on a guided tour.
cd:arapacis: Augustus's Altar of Peace, with its marble reliefs, in a glass pavilion by Richard Meier.
cd:doria: A private collection of Caravaggio, Velázquez and Titian in a palace that's still lived in.
cd:massimo: Statues, mosaics and the frescoes from Livia's villa: the finest Roman museum, near Termini.
cd:maxxi: Zaha Hadid's museum, with big curving spaces and art and architecture exhibitions.
cn:clemente: Basilica of San Clemente and excavations
cd:clemente: Three levels: a medieval basilica, below it a 4th-century church and further down a temple of Mithras.
cn:traiano: Trajan's Markets and Museum of the Imperial Forums
cd:traiano: Ancient Rome's great shopping centre, with shops and corridors still standing.
cd:vittoriano: The panoramic lift of the monument to Victor Emmanuel II: a 360-degree view of Rome.
cd:barberini: Bernini and Borromini's Baroque palace with Caravaggio, Raphael and Titian.
